S.R.Krishna Kumar, J., Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

Both these appeals arise out of the impugned judgment and award dated 27.04.2016 passed in M.V.C. No.833/2015 by the III Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ballari (for short, 'the Tribunal').
2.

entities.text: III Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ballari
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal.

3. Heard the learned counsel for the claimants and the learned counsel for the insurance company and perused the material on record.
4.

A perusal of the material on record discloses that the claimants are the mother, brother and grandparents of the deceased K.Phani Kumar who expired in a road traffic accident that occurred on 20.07.2015.

In the claim petition, it was specifically contended that at Durgamma Temple, near City Bus Stop, Ballari, when NC: 2023:KHC-D:10871-DB K.Phani Kumar got down from the bus and was going to meet his friend, the offending vehicle i.e., tipper lorry bearing registration No.KA-34/A-3923 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against him as a result of which he expired in the said accident.

It was contended that the deceased was aged about 21 years and brilliant in studies and he had completed the degree course in Bachelor of Computer Applications and was taking coaching to appear in Bank entrance examinations.

It was also contended that the deceased was a part-time worker in a private firm earning Rs.15,000/- per month and as such, the claimants are entitled to compensation towards the demise of the aforesaid K.Phani Kumar.
5.
Respondent No.1 is the driver, while respondent No.2 is the owner and respondent No.3 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Written statement was filed by respondents No.1 and 2 denying the claim of the claimants.

So also, respondent No.3-insurer also filed its statement of objections inter alia disputing the claim of the NC: 2023:KHC-D:10871-DB claimants and also contended that in the absence a valid and effective driving licence as well as the permit, the insurance company was not liable to pay the compensation.

Sri.K. Devaraja vs Smt.K. Vijayadurga on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155739884/
4 6.

After permitting all parties to adduce oral and documentary evidence, during the course of which the claimants examined P.W.1 and P.W.2 and marked Exs.P.1 to P.15, while respondent No.3-insurer examined R.W.1 and marked Exs.R.1 to R.4, the Tribunal came to conclusion that the accident in question resulting in the demise of K.Phani Kumar was on account of the rash and negligence driving of the driver of the tipper lorry.

However, insofar as the liability to pay compensation is concerned, the Tribunal came to the conclusion that the offending vehicle did not possess the valid permit as on the date of the accident and consequently exonerated/absolved the insurance company of its liability to pay compensation and fastened the entire liability to NC:
2023:KHC-D:10871-DB pay compensation upon the owner of the offending vehicle.

7. Aggrieved by the impugned judgment and award insofar as it relates to absolving/exonerating the insurance company to pay compensation and fastening the liability upon him, the owner of the offending vehicle viz., K.Devaraja i.e., respondent No.2 before the Tribunal has preferred M.F.A.
No.103139/2016.

So also, aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal and seeking enhancement, the claimants have preferred M.F.A. No.104178/2016.
8.

A perusal of the material on record will indicate that the sole ground on which the Tribunal has exonerated/absolved the respondent No.3-insurer of its liability to pay compensation is that as on the date of the accident that occurred on 20.07.2015, the offending vehicle did not possess a valid and effective permit.

In this regard, it is relevant to state that the said offending vehicle, in fact,
possessed permit which was valid from NC: 2023:KHC-D:10871-DB 11.06.2010 to 10.06.2015 and the same expired prior to the accident which occurred on 20.07.2015.

However, on 24.07.2015, the said permit, which stood expired, was subsequently renewed and would cover the period from 10.06.2015 onwards for a period of 5 years from 10.06.2015 onwards including 20.07.2015 when the accident occurred resulting in the demise of the aforesaid K.Phani Kumar.

In this context, it is relevant to note that the Tribunal has failed to consider Section 81(5) of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 which reads as under:
"81. Duration and renewal of permits.-

Where a permit has been renewed under this section after the expiry of the period thereof, such renewal shall have effect from the date of such expiry irrespective of whether or not a temporary permit has been granted under clause (d) of section 87, and where a temporary permit has been granted, the fee paid in respect of such temporary permit shall be refunded."

9. The aforesaid provision has been interpreted by a learned Single Judge of this Court in the case of The Divisional Manager, United India Insurance Co., Ltd., Vs. Kumar Bharthkumar [M.F.A.
No.24894/2012 and NC: 2023:KHC-D:10871-DB connected appeals, dated 17.09.2014] so as to create a legal fiction whereby the subsequent renewal of expired permit would relate back to the date of expiry and continue to remain in force and from the date of expiry onwards notwithstanding the fact that renewal was made at a subsequent in point of time.

sentences.text: In our considered opinion applying the law laid down by this Court in Bharthkumar's case, we are of the considered opinion that the Tribunal clearly fell in error in exonerating/absolving the insurance company of its liability to pay compensation and fastening the entire liability upon the owner of the offending vehicle and as such the impugned judgment and award in this regard deserves to be set aside.

Sri.K. Devaraja vs Smt.K. Vijayadurga on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155739884/
5 10.

Insofar as the quantum of compensation is concerned, a perusal of the material on record will indicate that the deceased K.Phani Kumar was a brilliant student and had completed the degree course in Bachelor of Computer Application and was undergoing coaching/tuition for banking entrance exams and the deceased K.Phani - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:10871-DB Kumar had the potential to earn higher income.

Under these circumstances, it would be just and appropriate to take the income of the deceased K.Phani Kumar as Rs.15,000/- per month, particularly, when the claimants had asserted that he was also doing a part-time job.
Accordingly, we take the income of the deceased at Rs.15,000/- per month.
11. The Tribunal has erred in applying the multiplier '14' considering the age of the mother of the deceased.

The Tribunal ought to have considered the age of the deceased while applying the multiplier, and since the deceased was aged 21 years as on the date of the accident, the appropriate multiplier applicable is '18'.
Since the deceased is bachelor, 50% of the income of the deceased is to be deducted towards his personal expenses.

Further, in view of the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi1, since the deceased was aged 21 years on the date 2017 ACJ 2700 - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:10871-DB of the accident, the claimants are entitled to addition of 40% of the income towards future prospects.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus, the claimants are entitled to a sum of Rs.22,68,000/-
[Rs.15,000/- + Rs.6,000/- (40% of Rs.15,000) = Rs.21,000 less 50% = Rs.10,500/- x 12 x 18] under the head 'loss of dependency'.
12.
The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.75,000/- under the conventional heads.

However,
compensation under the conventional heads has to be awarded as per the decisions of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited.
Vs. Pranay Sethi2 and in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Nau Ram & Ors.3.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the claimants are entitled to a sum of Rs.15,000/- each towards 'loss of estate' and 'funeral expenses'; and Rs.40,000/- each towards loss of consortium.

On re-assessment, the claimants are entitled total compensation as under:
1) Loss of dependency Rs. 22,68,000/-

claimant No.1 3) Loss of claimants No.2 to 4 Rs. 1,20,000/-
 4) Loss of estate Rs. 15,000/-
 5) Towards funeral expenses Rs. 15,000/-

Thus, the appellants-claimants are entitled to total compensation of Rs.24,58,000/- as against Rs.4,95,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal.
The enhanced compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.

14. In the result, we pass the following:
ORDER i) The appeal in M.F.A. No.103139/2016 filed by the owner is hereby allowed.
ii) M.F.A. No.104178/2016 filed by the claimants is hereby allowed in part.
iii) The impugned judgment and award, dated 27.04.2016, passed in M.V.C.
No.833/2015 by the Tribunal, insofar as it related to - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:10871-DB exonerating/absolving the respondent No.3- insurance company and fastening liability to pay compensation on respondent No.2-owner of the lorry, i.e., the appellant in M.F.A. No.103139/2016, is hereby set aside.
iv) It is held that respondent No.3-insurance company is liable to pay compensation in favour of the claimants.
v) The claimants are entitled to total compensation of Rs.24,58,000/- as against Rs.4,95,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal.
The enhanced compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization.

vi) The respondent No.3-insurance company (before the Tribubnal) shall deposit the aforesaid compensation along with interest within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.

7 vii)
On deposit of the amount by the Corporation, the same shall be apportioned among the claimants as per the award of the Tribunal.

The amount deposited by the appellant-Sri. K.Devaraja in M.F.A.
No.103139/2016 is directed to be refunded to the aforesaid appellant without any delay.
Registry to draw the award accordingly.
